programs.description: In alveolar type II cells, nascent surfactant protein precursors (SP-B and SP-C) are processed in intracellular compartments to yield mature surfactant peptides that reduce alveolar surface tension. Proteases NAPSA (napsin A) and CTSH (cathepsin H) cleave the N- and C-terminal domains of pro-SP-B and the N-terminal domain of pro-SP-C within multivesicular bodies and lamellar bodies, facilitating assembly of functional surfactant. This process is essential for surfactant homeostasis in lung alveoli.

atomic_biological_processes.name: Proteolytic processing of surfactant protein precursors

citation.reference: Brasch et al., J Biol Chem, 2003
citation.notes: Napsin A and Cathepsin H cleave pro-SP-B to generate mature SP-B and SP-C in type II cells ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14766755/#:~:text=SP,B%20peptide)).

citation.reference: Brasch et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2002
citation.notes: Cathepsin H mediates initial proteolytic processing of pro-SP-C in alveolar type II cells ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12034564/#:~:text=enzyme%20activities%20comparable%20to%20those,bodies%20of%20type%20II%20pneumocytes)).

citation.reference: Brasch et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2002
citation.notes: Cathepsin H and pro-SP-C are found in multivesicular bodies of type II cells ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12034564/#:~:text=enzyme%20activities%20comparable%20to%20those,bodies%20of%20type%20II%20pneumocytes)).

citation.reference: Matsuzaki et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2008
citation.notes: ABCA3 and surfactant-processing enzymes localize to lamellar bodies for surfactant storage; STAT3 deletion impairs lamellar body formation ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2335336/#:~:text=ATP,study%2C%20we%20demonstrate%20that%20STAT3)) ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2335336/#:~:text=role%20of%20STAT3%2C%20intratracheal%20IL,inhibited%20by%20deletion%20of%20Stat3)).

predicted_cellular_impact: Enables generation of mature SP-B and SP-C peptides for functional surfactant
Maintains alveolar stability by lowering surface tension
Supports packaging of surfactant into lamellar bodies
programs.evidence_summary: Napsin A (NAPSA) and Cathepsin H (CTSH) are proteases in alveolar type II cells that cleave pro-surfactant protein precursors. Studies show NAPSA cleaves the N- and C-terminal peptides of pro-SP-B and CTSH cleaves pro-SP-B and pro-SP-C, and knockdown of NAPSA reduces levels of mature SP-B and SP-C ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/13129928/#:~:text=napsin%20A%20in%20the%20processing,Two%20of%20the%20four)) ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14766755/#:~:text=fusion%20protein%2013%20amino%20acids,B%20peptide)). These processing steps occur in lamellar bodies and multivesicular bodies of type II pneumocytes, yielding active hydrophobic surfactant proteins that decrease surface tension in alveoli ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/13129928/#:~:text=napsin%20A%20in%20the%20processing,Two%20of%20the%20four)) ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12034564/#:~:text=enzyme%20activities%20comparable%20to%20those,bodies%20of%20type%20II%20pneumocytes)).

citations.reference: Brasch et al., J Biol Chem, 2003
citations.notes: Napsin A and Cathepsin H cleavage of pro-SP-B and pro-SP-C in alveolar type II cells ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14766755/#:~:text=SP,B%20peptide)).

citations.reference: Brasch et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2002
citations.notes: Cathepsin H is required for processing of pro-SP-C in type II cells ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12034564/#:~:text=enzyme%20activities%20comparable%20to%20those,bodies%20of%20type%20II%20pneumocytes)).

programs.program_name: Surfactant lipid transport and lamellar body formation
programs.description: ABCA3 is a lamellar body membrane lipid transporter in alveolar type II cells that imports phospholipids into lamellar bodies for surfactant assembly. This process enables formation of functional phospholipid-rich surfactant and proper lamellar body biogenesis. Dysfunctional ABCA3 leads to defective lamellar bodies, altered surfactant composition, and impaired alveolar surface tension regulation.

citation.reference: Matsuzaki et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2008
citation.notes: Describes ABCA3 as a lamellar body lipid transporter essential for normal surfactant lipid uptake in type II cells ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2335336/#:~:text=ATP,study%2C%20we%20demonstrate%20that%20STAT3)).

atomic_biological_processes.name: Lamellar body assembly and surfactant storage

citation.reference: Matsuzaki et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2008
citation.notes: Shows that STAT3-regulated ABCA3 expression influences lamellar body formation in type II cells ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2335336/#:~:text=ATP,study%2C%20we%20demonstrate%20that%20STAT3)) ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2335336/#:~:text=role%20of%20STAT3%2C%20intratracheal%20IL,inhibited%20by%20deletion%20of%20Stat3)).

citation.reference: Shulenin et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2004
citation.notes: Immunohistochemistry shows ABCA3 localizes to the limiting membrane of lamellar bodies in type II cells ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11718719/#:~:text=membrane%20fraction%20of%20human%20lung,surfactant%20in%20type%20II%20cells)).

predicted_cellular_impact: Promotes lamellar body formation and surfactant storage
programs.evidence_summary: ABCA3 is exclusively expressed in lung alveolar type II cells and localizes to lamellar body membranes ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11718719/#:~:text=membrane%20fraction%20of%20human%20lung,surfactant%20in%20type%20II%20cells)). It transports phospholipids into lamellar bodies, enabling surfactant biogenesis. Genetic deficiency of ABCA3 leads to smaller lamellar bodies, altered surfactant lipid composition, and respiratory failure in neonates ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2335336/#:~:text=ATP,study%2C%20we%20demonstrate%20that%20STAT3)) ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10786693/#:~:text=Mutations%20in%20ATP,with%20pathological%20variants%20of%20ABCA3)).

citations.reference: Matsuzaki et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2008
citations.notes: ABCA3 is a lamellar body-associated lipid transporter required for normal surfactant synthesis and storage ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2335336/#:~:text=ATP,study%2C%20we%20demonstrate%20that%20STAT3)).

citations.reference: Shulenin et al., Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol, 2004
citations.notes: Shows ABCA3 localization to lamellar bodies in alveolar type II cells ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11718719/#:~:text=membrane%20fraction%20of%20human%20lung,surfactant%20in%20type%20II%20cells)).
